title: Amba's Retribution
body:
Amba's Retribution

Satyavati bore Shantanu two sons: Chitrangada and Vichitravirya. Chitrangada, the elder, was a proud and powerful warrior who was killed in a long combat with a Gandharva of the same name. Vichitravirya, still a youth, succeeded him. When the time came for Vichitravirya's marriage, Bheeshma heard of the Swayamvara of the three princesses of Kashi—Amba, Ambika, and Ambalika. Bheeshma went to Kashi, challenged the assembled princes, defeated them all, and carried the three sisters away in his chariot to Hastinapur.
Before they reached the capital, King Salva of Saubala, who was secretly loved by Amba, opposed Bheeshma. Bheeshma defeated Salva but spared his life at the sisters' request. Arriving in Hastinapur, as preparations were underway for the wedding, Amba approached Bheeshma and said: 'O son of Ganga, I have mentally chosen Salva as my husband. You have brought me here by force. Knowing this, do what is righteous according to the scriptures.'
Bheeshma, acknowledging the justice of her plea, sent Amba to Salva with a honorable escort. However, Salva rejected her, saying: 'Bheeshma defeated me in the sight of all and carried you away. I have been disgraced. I cannot receive you as my wife now. Return to him and do as he commands.' Amba returned to Hastinapur in tears, but Vichitravirya refused to marry her because her heart had been given to another.
Rejected by both, Amba's grief turned into burning hatred, and she identified Bheeshma as the sole cause of her ruin. She sought the aid of Sage Parasurama, Bheeshma's preceptor. Moved by her anguish, Parasurama engaged in a long and equal combat with Bheeshma. In the end, Parasurama had to acknowledge defeat, advising Amba to throw herself on Bheeshma's mercy.
Amba refused. She retired to the forest, performing extreme austerities to obtain a boon from Lord Shiva. Receiving a divine garland of ever-fresh lotuses, she was promised that whoever wore the garland would become the instrument of Bheeshma's death. After hanging the garland on King Drupada's palace gate, she threw herself into a sacrificial fire and was reborn as Drupada's daughter, Sikhandin, who eventually became a male warrior and stood as Arjuna's shield to bring about Bheeshma's fall at Kurukshetra.
